messages.subject: Pull requests
parts:
Hi everyone -

As you may know, I've been hired to work on ggplot2 full time. Part of my job is to reduce Hadley's load by handling pull requests, and I think this is a good time for me to explain how I'll try to do this.

At this point I can handle small, simple pull requests, and bug fixes in areas where I'm knowledgable. The areas that I'm able to cover will grow as I gain more experience and become more comfortable with the code.

Generally speaking, new features will have to be vetted by Hadley, since he has a better idea of how things should work, and where ggplot2 is headed.

Sometimes pull requests will sit around for weeks or even months. Don't worry -- this doesn't mean they're forgotten. It probably means that Hadley needs to sit down and take a close look at it.


I may also do some rebasing of pull requests to keep a neater, easier-to-follow commit tree.
- For some pull requests, especially very small ones, I may rebase the commit right onto the master branch, without a merge commit. This will keep a simpler commit tree, which is easier to understand, and helpful for finding bugs.
- If you have an open pull request, I may also ask you to rebase it (or do it myself) onto master.
- I may also ask you to squash some of the commits together (or do it myself). This is useful when you work on a branch where the early commits are rough and experimental, and are refined in later commits. In cases like this, keeping the early commits in the main ggplot2 repo can actually be detrimental for understanding the history of the code and for finding bugs, so it can make sense to squash the commits together before merging into master.


-Winston
